true_effects.expected_conclusion: Women cross QTc outlier categories more often mainly because of longer baseline QTc (and are more TdP-prone at equal QTc); the drug's effect per unit concentration does not differ by sex. Monitoring, not dose, is the Phase II question.
true_effects.background_terms: Dizziness, fatigue, headache, nausea, palpitations: no drug or sex effect (illustrative rates)
true_effects.note: Torsade de pointes is rare; a trial of this size usually has 0-2 cases, too few for a sex comparison.

sotalol.finding: TdP 4.1% of women vs 1.9% of men; ~3x adjusted odds, not explained by dose or bradycardia
sources: Lehmann MH et al. Circulation 1996 (22 trials, 3,135 adults)

ibutilide.finding: TdP 5.6% of women vs 3.0% of men; larger QTc increase in women (59-63 vs 46 ms, low dose)

dofetilide.finding: Women dose-reduced or stopped more often (55% vs 32%); TdP more frequent in women; no sex difference in exposure-adjusted QTc in healthy volunteers
sources: Vicente J et al. J Electrocardiol 2015;48(6):1081-7

quinidine.finding: No sex difference in exposure-adjusted QTc prolongation
sources: Vicente J et al. J Electrocardiol 2015

class_overview.finding: 70% (95% CI 64-75%) of 332 published cardiovascular-drug TdP cases were women (case reports; reporting bias)

baseline_qtc.finding: Post-pubertal women have longer baseline QTc than men (about 8-10 ms in one multi-formula study)
sources: Rautaharju PM et al. Can J Cardiol 1992

dqtc_magnitude.finding: Mean QTc +19 +/- 30 ms after initial sotalol/dofetilide dose; +11 +/- 37 ms for sotalol at >=48 h

max_qtc_initiation.finding: Mean maximal QTc 471 ms during sotalol/dofetilide initiation with standard dosing (517 ms with non-standard)

regulatory_categories.finding: QTcF > 450/480/500 ms and increase > 30/60 ms categorical analysis; >500 or >60 commonly used to stop dosing
